summary.tldr: Prohibits fur farming and related activities, and creates offences, penalties and forfeiture rules for breaking the ban.
what_it_does: Prohibits owning or operating a fur farm, breeding or inseminating fur-bearing animals for fur farms, slaughtering them for their pelts, or giving, renting, selling or transporting them to a fur farm.
Creates offences for breaking those rules, with fines of up to $250,000 or prison for up to two years on indictment, or fines of up to $50,000 or prison for up to six months on summary conviction.
Allows courts to bar an offender from owning, having custody or control of, or living in the same place as an animal for a period the court sets.
Allows courts to order an offender to pay reasonable care costs to a person or organisation that took care of a fur-bearing animal because of the offence.
Allows the Governor in Council to make regulations for a compensation regime for losses from complying with the Act, and makes the Act start one year after royal assent.
summary.background: A fur farm is defined as a place where fur-bearing animals are kept in captivity so their pelts can be used for commercial purposes.
